method_name: Diff Mining (top-K occurrence + NMF token topics)

parameters.tokenization: raw text, no chat template, add_special_tokens=False, first T tokens

deviations_from_paper.reference_corpus: The repository's clean reference prompts (held-out Tulu-style instruction user strings, fed as raw text without a chat template) instead of the authors' pretraining-text sample (config: science-of-finetuning/fineweb-1m-sample; paper: 'random webtext', e.g. FineWeb).
deviations_from_paper.n_documents: All retained reference prompts (276 for the shared set) instead of the paper's default N=1000 (Appendix C) or the code default max_samples=8192.
deviations_from_paper.positions_per_document: T=30, the paper default (Appendix C); the code default max_tokens_per_sample is 64.
deviations_from_paper.tokenization: tok(text, add_special_tokens=False, truncation=True, max_length=T) as in the original M3 run; the authors use tok.encode(text[:10*T], add_special_tokens=True)[:T]. The Qwen3.5 tokenizer adds no BOS, and both give identical first-30 token IDs for all 276 shared reference prompts (checked when this module was written).
deviations_from_paper.logit_diff_precision: Logits are upcast to float32 before subtraction (original M3 run). The authors subtract in the models' output dtype (bfloat16 for bfloat16 models), which can change top-K membership for near-ties at the K-th value.
deviations_from_paper.batching: One prompt per forward pass by default (original M3 run); the authors batch 16 right-padded documents with an attention mask. Retained documents all have exactly T tokens, so there are no padding positions either way.
deviations_from_paper.nmf_solver: torchnmf 0.3.5 NMF.fit (sparse V, beta=2 multiplicative updates, tol=1e-4, max_iter=200) is re-implemented in closed form in plain torch because torchnmf is not a dependency. Updates, eps handling, update order (W then H), loss definition and stopping rule follow the torchnmf source.
deviations_from_paper.nmf_initialisation: W then H drawn as |N(0,1)| from a dedicated CPU torch.Generator seeded with the run seed (torchnmf draws them the same way from the global torch RNG, which the authors seed once with cfg.seed=42 at pipeline start and which other code then consumes), so the authors' exact initialisation cannot be reproduced.
deviations_from_paper.nmf_device: NMF runs on CPU in float32; the authors run it on CUDA when available.
deviations_from_paper.nmf_extra_seeds: Not in the paper or the writeup: the primary NMF configuration is refitted from seed + 1..4 to measure initialization sensitivity; the primary fit is unchanged.
deviations_from_paper.nmf_tokens_per_topic: 100 tokens per topic: the authors' code writes num_tokens = max(visualization.num_tokens_to_plot=100, top_k=100) tokens per topic; the config field top_n_tokens_per_topic=200 is only used in the output directory name. Scores at 200 tokens per topic are reported too.
deviations_from_paper.nmf_num_topics: 3 topics (authors' config default). The paper says the number of topics depends on the use case and Appendix G.3 used 5, so 5 is reported as a sensitivity fit.
deviations_from_paper.no_llm_interpretation: No LLM token-relevance grader (authors: gpt-5-mini) and no interpretability agent. Token lists are scored with trojan_diffing.common.score_tokens on token IDs. Full trigger/payload recovery is impossible from token lists.
deviations_from_paper.orderings_not_reported: The authors' fraction_positive_diff ordering and top-K negative counts are not reported (per-token sum of diffs and positive counts are saved in the artifact).
deviations_from_paper.logit_extraction: Direct output logits (the config's logit_extraction.method default). The authors' agent-overview default reads a patchscope-lens variant, which is not run.
deviations_from_paper.topk_occurrence_tie_breaking: Count ties broken by first occurrence (collections.Counter.most_common, as in the original M3 run); the authors' torch.topk over occurrence rates leaves tie order unspecified.

matrix.definition: rows = analysed positions (prompt-major, position-minor); columns = tokens in any row's top-K (authors' first-appearance order); entry = ReLU(logit_ft - logit_base) for the row's top-K tokens, 0 elsewhere

summary.full_recovery_note: Both orderings output single tokens; the trigger and payload are multi-token strings, so full recovery is impossible by construction.

train_meta.throughput_scope: estimated from actual segment epochs and the first 500 row lengths
